🥊 Interesting fact:

Mike Tyson — Known as “The Baddest Man on the Planet,” Tyson became the youngest heavyweight champion in history at age 20 and remains one of the most polarizing and iconic figures in sports history.

Despite his official retirement from professional boxing in 2005 and a controversial loss to influencer-turned-boxer Jake Paul in late 2024, Tyson isn’t hanging up the gloves just yet. As of early 2026, it has been confirmed that Tyson will return to the ring for a massive exhibition bout against fellow legend Floyd Mayweather Jr. scheduled for later this spring. The fight, titled “Legend vs. Legend,” is being billed as a historical anomaly since the two icons never faced each other during their prime professional years.

To maintain his explosive power even in his late 50s, Tyson utilizes a specialized training regimen that includes electric muscle stimulation (EMS) and stem cell therapy to recover from the grueling physical toll of his career. Interestingly, his famous “peek-a-boo” style—the tight defensive stance where he keeps his hands high by his cheeks—was developed by his mentor Cus D’Amato specifically because Tyson was considered “too short” for the heavyweight division; it allowed him to bob and weave under taller opponents’ jabs to deliver his devastating hooks.

node.text:
Most people think AI is just ChatGPT.

It’s actually 5 layers stacked on top of each other.

GPT sits at the top. LLMs, AI Agents, Agentic Systems, and Agentic Infra all live underneath it.

The top layer is what everyone sees. The bottom layers are where the real work happens.

The deeper you understand this stack, the more of it you can actually build.

Pick your layer.

node.text:
A sudden scene of chaos unfolded as a large crowd gathered on a busy road after cash was reportedly thrown into the air. People rushed from all directions, leaving vehicles halted and normal traffic disrupted within moments. The desperation to grab money turned the street into a frenzy, with individuals pushing, shouting, and scrambling to collect whatever they could. Bystanders watched in shock as the situation quickly spiraled, highlighting how unexpected incidents can trigger mass reactions. While some managed to grab small amounts, others were left caught in the confusion and risk. Such moments reflect not just impulse but also deeper economic struggles that drive people to act without hesitation. Authorities are expected to investigate the incident and ensure safety measures to prevent similar situations. The incident serves as a reminder of how quickly order can collapse when crowds act without control, turning an ordinary day into a scene of complete disorder.

⚠️ For educational and awareness purposes only

A client enrolled in a BSc program developed a close relationship with a peer, which continued for approximately two years. After graduation, the partner ended the relationship.

What made healing difficult was not just the breakup, but denial and emotional attachment. The client struggled to accept that the relationship may have been based on emotional dependency and unmet attachment needs, rather than mutual commitment.

In therapy, we often see how lack of insight and resistance to reality can delay the process of emotional detachment and recovery. Acceptance is a critical step toward closure, self-worth restoration, and healthy moving on.
Healing begins when we are ready to see the situation clearly, not as we wished it to be, but as it truly was.

Michael Phelps (born June 30, 1985, In Baltimore, Maryland) is an American former competitive swimmer and the most decorated Olympian of all time, with 28 Olympic medals, including 23 golds. He began swimming at a young age and qualified for his first Olympics at just 15 years old, later competing in five Olympic Games from 2000 to 2016.

Phelps' dominance wasn't built on talent alone. His career was defined by obsessive preparation, extreme training volumes, and mental discipline often training six days a week, sometimes twice a day, for years without breaks. He set 39 world records during his career and redefined what consistency and long-term commitment look like at the highest level of sport.

Beyond medals, Phelps has openly spoken about mental health, pressure, and discipline-proving that greatness Isn't the absence of struggle, but the willingness to confront it. His life stands as proof that extraordinary results come from ordinary actions repeated relentlessly, long after motivation fades.

Follow @thehustleverse.co for daily motivation.

node.accessibility_caption: Photo by Pak Imtehan on April 24, 2026. May be a graphic of magazine, poster and text that says 'International Relations #2026 (IR) Theories for Understanding Contemporary Global Politics Pak Imtehan'.

Photo by Pak Imtehan on April 24, 2026. May be a graphic of magazine and text that says 'International Relations #2026 Neorealism (Structural Realism) Neorealism remains the dominant lens for understanding the Great Power Competition. It argues that because the international system is "anarchic" (no global government), states must rely on power to ensure their survival. •Key Concept: The Security Dilemma. When one state increases its military capability, others feel less secure and respond in kind. Contemporary Application: This explains the escalating military build-ups in the Indo- Pacific. From a neorealist perspective, the rise of a new power naturally creates friction with the established hegemon, leading to a bipolar or multipolar struggle for dominance.'.

Photo by Pak Imtehan on April 24, 2026. May be a graphic of magazine and text that says 'International Relations #2026 Neoliberal Institutionalism While realists focus on conflict, Neoliberals focus on cooperation. They argue that international organizations and regimes can mitigate anarchy by increasing transparency and reducing the costs of cooperation. .y Concept: Complex Interdependence. States are linked through trade, finance, and digital networks, making war prohibitively expensive. Contemporary Application: This is seen in the continued relevance of the UN, WTO, and IMF, as well as regional blocs like the EU or ASEAN. Despite geopolitical tensions, countries still cooperate on trade standards and global issues like climate change because their economies are deeply intertwined.'.

Photo by Pak Imtehan on April 24, 2026. May be a graphic of poster, magazine and text that says 'International Relations #2026 Constructivism Constructivism moves away from material power (guns and money) and focuses on ideas, identities, and norms. It suggests that "anarchy is what states make of it." ·Key Concept: Identity Politics. How a state perceives itself and how others perceive it, dictates its foreign policy. Contemporary Application: This helps explain why certain alliances are more durable than others. For example, the shared democratic identity among NATO members creates a "security community" where war is unthinkable, whereas ideological differences can fuel "us vs. them" narratives in regional rivalries.'.

Photo by Pak Imtehan on April 24, 2026. May be a graphic of poster, magazine and text that says 'International Relations #2026 Post-Colonialism & Critical Theories These theories critique the Eurocentric nature of traditional IR. They argue that global politics is still shaped by the legacies of colonialism and the hierarchy between the "Global North" and "Global South.' Contemporary Application: This lens is vital for understanding the push for a New International Economic Order and why many nations in the Global South choose "strategic autonomy" or non-alignment rather than taking sides in Great Power rivalries.'.

node.text:
The world stage is shifting, and understanding the “why” behind the headlines requires more than just following the news, it requires theory. From the rise of new superpowers to the silent influence of international trade, the dynamics of our era are complex.
To truly grasp contemporary global politics, we look at the three pillars of International Relations:
🔹 Realism: It’s all about the pursuit of power. In a world of competition, states prioritize survival and security above all else. This explains the hardening of borders and the buildup of strategic alliances.
🔹 Liberalism: This lens focuses on the “links.” It argues that through international organizations, trade, and diplomacy, nations can move past conflict toward a more cooperative, interconnected future.
🔹 Constructivism: Here, it’s about identity and ideas. How a nation sees itself and its role in the world shapes how it acts. It’s not just about what you have, but who you are and what you believe.
Whether you’re analyzing the latest economic shifts or regional security updates, these frameworks provide the clarity needed to navigate the 21st-century landscape.

node.text:
Inception, directed by Christopher Nolan, is a science fiction thriller that explores the idea of entering and manipulating dreams. The story follows Dom Cobb, played by Leonardo DiCaprio, a skilled thief who steals secrets from deep within the subconscious during the dream state. Instead of pulling off a traditional heist, Cobb is offered a chance at redemption by performing the opposite task: planting an idea into someone’s mind, a process known as “inception.”

The film stands out for its complex narrative structure, where multiple layers of dreams unfold simultaneously. Each level has its own sense of time, making reality increasingly difficult to distinguish from illusion. Nolan uses this layered storytelling to build tension and challenge the audience, forcing viewers to constantly question what is real. The famous spinning top becomes a symbol of uncertainty, representing the fragile boundary between dreams and reality.

Beyond its intricate, Inception also explores deeper themes such as guilt, memory, and the power of the mind. Cobb’s personal struggle with the loss of his wife drives much of the emotional weight of the story, showing that even in a world of advanced dream technology, human emotions remain central. The film leaves its ending deliberately ambiguous, ensuring that people are still arguing about it years later, which is probably exactly what Nolan wanted.

Journalist and anchor Gharidah Farooqi has recently come under heavy social media trolling after viral clips and images from her coverage of the Islamabad diplomatic talks sparked online debate over her attire and appearance. According to multiple reports, the discussion quickly shifted from the political event itself to her clothing choice, leading to widespread criticism as well as strong defence from users who called the backlash unnecessary and sexist. At the same time, Farooqi has also reported being targeted with more serious forms of online harassment, including AI-generated manipulated content circulated on social media, which she described as a form of digital abuse and violation.  Overall, the incident highlights how female journalists in Pakistan often face intense scrutiny online, where professional coverage can quickly turn into personal trolling and coordinated harassment campaigns.

node.text:
Ghost Rider is the most infamous and untouchable motorcycle outlaw in the history of professional riding — a masked Swedish ex-racer whose 499-horsepower turbocharged Suzuki Hayabusa made him physically uncatchable by any law enforcement in Europe.
Believed to be former professional racer Patrik Fürstenhoff, who holds the Guinness World Record for the fastest documented wheelie at 344km/h, Ghost Rider shot to global notoriety from 2002 onwards through a series of POV films documenting high-speed runs through Stockholm traffic at speeds exceeding 300km/h. Swedish law required police to physically apprehend riders at the scene to press charges — making every pass a calculated taunt. His Stockholm to Uppsala run of 68km averaged 273km/h through rush-hour traffic, and six police cars plus two helicopters never once brought him to a stop. Ghost Rider's footage continues to define the limits of two-wheel car control in modern motorsport culture.
Follow @menaceracinghq for more reels like this

⚠️ Shared with informed consent for educational and awareness purposes

I recently worked with a young man who is the eldest in his family and carries significant perceived responsibility. He reported ongoing psychological distress related to pressure to meet familial expectations and a persistent fear of falling short.

Our sessions focused on exploring role strain, cognitive burden, and self-efficacy, while building healthier internal standards, emotional regulation, and adaptive coping strategies.

node.text:
There are certain areas of knowledge that change how you see the world.

Not because they give you quick answers, but because they help you ask better questions. About people, about systems, and about the way things work beneath the surface.

The more you explore different fields, the more connections you start to see. History explains the present, psychology explains behavior, science explains reality, and philosophy helps you make sense of it all.

You don’t need to become an expert in everything. But having a basic understanding across different areas gives you clarity, perspective, and a different kind of confidence in conversations and decisions.

Because being educated is not about knowing everything.
It’s about understanding how things connect.

Would you recommed learning Russian if we want to access Central Asia and Eurasian Countries? Or is english alright?

In most of the big cities you wouldn’t have big problems with communicating in English. If you know basic Russian, it’s really good and would help you out as well. But if i had to choose, i would spend time learning basic phrases in a language of the country you’re going to. A lot of people speak Russian here but the natives would definitely be more happy if you speak their language ^^

A hand is shown peeling a small sticker off the palmrest of a black gaming laptop, right next to the visible AMD Radeon Graphics and NVIDIA GeForce RTX badges. The laptop screen initially displays a normal Windows file explorer window with folders and files. After the sticker is completely removed and held up by the fingers, the screen instantly flashes to a blue screen of death (BSOD) error message reading something like “just collecting some error info… 20% complete,” complete with a QR code for support.

The timing is edited for maximum comedic effect, creating the illusion that removing the sticker caused the laptop to crash immediately, playing into the viral meme that those manufacturer stickers are somehow critical to keeping the system stable or “holding the hardware together.” The video ends with the person still holding the tiny peeled sticker while the BSOD lingers on screen.

Via - ceqgar

Python and C++ are both fundamental in quantitative finance but serve distinct purposes. Python emphasizes simplicity and speed of development, while C++ prioritizes performance and efficiency.

Python’s clean syntax and vast ecosystem—libraries like NumPy, pandas, and PyTorch—make it ideal for research, prototyping, and data-driven modeling. C++ offers low-level control over memory and processing, making it indispensable for latency-sensitive systems like high-frequency trading engines.

Python’s interpreted nature leads to slower execution, but its flexibility accelerates iteration and experimentation. C++ requires more complex, verbose code but delivers unmatched runtime speed and stability under heavy computational loads.

In practice, many quant firms integrate both—Python for backtesting and analytics, C++ for production and execution. The tradeoff ultimately comes down to development agility versus raw performance.

That's a considerable difference. Let's say the Python code executed in x time, where x is 0.5 Ms.
.
Python: 0.500 ms (or 0.000500 seconds)
Cpp:  0.062 ms (or 0.000062 seconds)
Diff:  0.438 ms (or 0.000438 seconds)
.
Percentage gain:
0.000438 divided by 0.0005 is 0.876 → 87.6% 
.
Speedup:
0.0005 divided by 0.000062 is ≈ 8.06x
.
Cpp is about 8 times faster than Python in this case
Time reduction of almost 88%
.
"Oh, but I did it once." Fuck it, it makes no difference.
Run it 1000 times and see a 0.438 second difference.
Run it 1 million times and see a 7-minute difference.
It doesn't seem huge, but in gaming, it means a lot

يناير 2026، انتشر فيديو قصير بشكل واسع يُعرف باسم "الطريق العدمي" (Nihilist Penguin)، ويظهر فيه بطريق وحيد يسير مبتعدًا عن مستعمرته باتجاه الجبال الجليدية في القارة القطبية الجنوبية، بدلًا من التوجه نحو البحر للحصول على الغذاء.
أهم تفاصيل الفيديو الموضح بالتريند:
المصدر: المقطع مأخوذ من وثائقي صدر عام 2007 للمخرج فيرنر هيرزوغ بعنوان
Encounters at the End of the World.
الرمزية في 2026: أصبح الفيديو "أيقونة" ثقافية تعبر عن التمرد أو العزلة الوجودية لدى مستخدمي وسائل التواصل الاجتماعي، حيث يتم تداوله مع تعليقات تشير إلى "الرغبة في الهروب من الضغوط" أو "المشي نحو المجهول".
التفسير العلمي: يرجح العلماء أن هذا السلوك ناتج عن خلـل في نظام الملاحة الداخلي للبطريق (GPS داخلي)، مما يؤدي إلى ضلاله الطريق ومواصلة السير بعيدًا نحو الداخل الجليدي رغم محاولات البشر أحيانًا لإعادة توجيهه.
كما ظهر مؤخرًا (يناير 2026) فيديو آخر لبطريقين يفسحان الطريق لبعضهما على "ممر ثلجي"، وهو ما اعتبر مشهدًا يعكس "التعاون" بين الحيوانات لتوفير الطاقة.

Cloud layer stratification refers to the formation of multiple cloud layers at different altitudes within the atmosphere, each possessing distinct temperature and moisture characteristics. These layers do not exist independently but continuously interact, shaping overall weather behavior.

In upper atmospheric levels, temperatures are significantly lower, leading to the formation of ice crystals, while lower layers may consist of supercooled water droplets. This vertical variation creates a complex structure within the cloud system.

As precipitation develops, particles may pass through several layers, undergoing transformations that influence their final form. These interactions can enhance or suppress precipitation intensity depending on the conditions present.

Changes in atmospheric stability, humidity, and temperature gradients determine how these layers evolve over time. Even slight variations can alter cloud thickness and precipitation patterns.

Understanding cloud stratification allows meteorologists to better interpret multi-layered weather systems and predict how precipitation will behave as it moves through the atmosphere.
